sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Membrane localization confirmed by immunofluorescence (surface_only). ErbB4 activation is reported for NRG4 variants with an intact EGF-like domain, but this functional assay is not explicitly attributed to the GFP-tagged construct itself.
sites.rationale: NRG4 is a Type I single-pass protein with its N-terminus extracellular (residues 1–60) and C-terminus intracellular (residues 83–115); there is no signal peptide, so residue 1 (M) is the first extracellular residue. The ledger names no junction residue and no terminus explicitly, but the protein has exactly one extracellular terminus, so a surface-displayed GFP must be prepended before residue 1 (insert_after_residue = 0). Python confirms residue_after = 'M' (seq[0]). The N-terminal prepend is ≥3 residues from the TM boundary (TM begins at residue 61) and does not contact the six disulfide-forming cysteines (positions 9, 17, 23, 34, 36, 45) of the EGF-like domain. GFP-tagged NRG4 A1 (full-length, containing the predicted transmembrane region) transfected into Cos-7 cells and confirmed to localize to the plasma membrane by immunofluorescence. No junction residue is named in any ledger line.

sources.claim:
In transfected cells, the A type variant (NRG4 A1) was localized to the membrane, whereas the B type variant (NRG4 B1), which lacks the predicted transmembrane region, had an intracellular localization. Only the variants with an intact epidermal growth factor-like domain activated ErbB4 signaling.

Conclusion

NRG4 overexpression is associated with advanced-stage prostate cancer. The alternative splice variants may have different roles in cell signaling, some acting as classic receptor ligands and some with as-yet unknown functions.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe GFP-tagged full-length NRG4 A1 expressed in mammalian cells and confirmed at the plasma membrane, but none specifies whether GFP is N- or C-terminal, nor any junction residue. The topology_derived rule is applied: NRG4 has exactly one extracellular terminus (N-terminus, residues 1–60), so a surface-displayed GFP must be an N-terminal prepend. L1 (PMID 17684490) and L2 (PMID 17545517) provide corroborating evidence for the same finding; L3 (PMID 17545517) is the most informative and is used as the single supporting clip. No ledger line supports any internal loop insertion, and no ledger line specifies a C-terminal tag. The intracellular C-terminus (residues 83–115) is not a surface site and is not proposed. No function-abrogating insertions are reported in the ledger.
